The projected cycle life of these electrolyte classes is anticipated to be sufficiently high and comparable for long-duration storage; therefore, it is not included as a differentiating axis in this comparison. For the anode, we must confront a controversial question: is lithium metal necessary or even desirable for ESS? The associated complex­ ities—infinite relative volume change, stringent pressure requirements, and the perpetual risk of dendrite propagation—introduce massive cost, manufacturing, and longevity challenges that may fundamentally un­ dermine its value proposition. A more pragmatic path is the adoption of silicon-based anodes (e.g., SiOx-C composites and pure Si) [32].
